Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're experiencing as a new mother, and I'm committed to supporting you through this journey. As part of our conversation, I'll be using the EPDS to help us understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a valuable tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during this time. It's essential to note that this assessment is not a diagnosis, but rather a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your feelings and concerns.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I'm here to create a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings without judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional state over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you'd like.

Let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. I'd like to ask: Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to, or has that been a bit more challenging for you lately?

.. to be honest, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things like I used to. I mean, I still smile and laugh when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and laughing doesn't come as naturally as it used to. Even when I do laugh, it feels a bit forced, like I'm trying to convince myself that everything is okay when it's not. I've been feeling really overwhelmed and anxious, and it's hard to see the funny side of things when I'm worried about my baby's safety all the time. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy for my baby's sake, but deep down, I'm just feeling really sad and discouraged. It's like the joy has been sucked out of me, and I don't know how to get it back. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say the same. Like I said, it's just been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just so tired and worried all the time, and it's hard to laugh when you're feeling that way. I mean, my baby is adorable and she does make me smile, but it's not the same as laughing and feeling carefree like I used to. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, and I'm not really experiencing the joy that I thought I would. It's like, I'll be playing with my baby and she'll do something cute, and I'll smile, but then I'll just start worrying about something else, like is she eating enough or is she developing okay... and it just takes over. It's hard to explain, but it feels like my brain is just consumed by all these worries and fears, and it's hard to shake them off.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my baby or a visit with a friend, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but when the time comes, I just don't feel like doing it. I'll feel too tired, or too anxious, or just overwhelmed. And even when I do manage to get out and do something, I don't always enjoy it as much as I thought I would. It's like, I'll be at the park with my baby, and I'll see all these other moms laughing and chatting, and I'll feel like I'm just not a part of it. I'll feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I'm not really experiencing any joy. Sometimes I'll even find myself feeling guilty for not enjoying things as much as I think I should. Like, I'll think, "What's wrong with me? I'm a new mom, I should be happy and excited," but the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way most of the time. It's hard to explain, but it feels like my interest in things has just... dwindled, I guess. I don't feel like myself anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's something I've been doing a lot of lately. I feel like I'm always wondering if I'm doing something wrong, or if I'm not doing enough for my baby. Like, if she's crying, I'll think, "Oh, it's because I'm not feeding her right," or "I'm not changing her diaper often enough." Even when my husband or my mom tries to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't shake the feeling that I'm somehow failing my baby. And it's not just about the big things, it's about the little things too. Like, if I'm trying to get her to sleep and she won't settle down, I'll think, "It's because I'm not doing the right routine," or "I'm not creating a soothing enough environment." It's like, I'm always second-guessing myself and wondering if I'm good enough. And sometimes, when things go really wrong, like if I have a hard time getting her to latch or something, I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of guilt and shame. I'll think, "I'm a terrible mother," or "I'm not cut out for this." It's really hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just constantly criticizing myself and wondering if I'm doing everything wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been me lately. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the house catches on fire, or what if someone breaks in. It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of worry and fear. And it's not just about big things, it's about little things too. Like, I'll worry that my baby is too hot or too cold, or that she's not eating enough. Even when my husband or my mom tries to reassure me that everything is fine, I just can't shake the feeling that something is off.

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of anxiety. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to panic. It's like, I'm trapped in this never-ending cycle of worry and fear, and I don't know how to escape. And the worst part is, I know it's irrational. I know that most of the things I'm worrying about are unlikely to happen. But that doesn't stop my mind from racing, and it doesn't stop me from feeling anxious and scared.

It's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always on high alert, and I just can't relax. Even when I'm doing things that I used to enjoy, like taking a bath or reading a book, I'll just start worrying about something, and it'll ruin the whole experience. It's like, I'm just stuck in this state of constant anxiety, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, my body just takes over, and I feel like I'm not in control anymore. And the worst part is, it's not even like I'm thinking about anything scary or stressful at the time. It's just like, out of nowhere, this feeling of panic and fear will hit me.

Sometimes, it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start worrying that something is going to happen to her. I'll think, "What if I'm not paying attention, and she rolls off the couch?" or "What if I'm not feeding her enough?" And then, my mind will just start spiraling out of control, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of panic. Other times, it happens when I'm trying to fall asleep, and I'll just lie there, feeling like I'm on edge, waiting for something to go wrong.

It's hard to explain, but it feels like my body is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to trigger this panic response. And when it happens, it's like, I'm frozen in fear, and I don't know how to calm myself down. My husband will try to talk to me, and I'll just shake my head, because I don't know how to explain what's happening. It's like, I'm trapped in this cycle of fear and panic, and I don't know how to escape.

I do remember one time, I was feeding my baby, and she started crying, and I just felt this wave of panic wash over me. I thought, "Oh no, what's wrong with her? Is she okay?" And then, my mind just started racing, and I felt like I was going to pass out. It was like, my body just took over, and I was no longer in control. It was really scary, and it's happened a few times since then. I just wish I could find a way to calm myself down and stop these panic attacks from happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. It's like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's all just feeling so overwhelming. I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities, and I don't know how to stay afloat.

Some days, I'll wake up feeling okay, and then by the end of the day, I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. The baby will be crying, and I'll be exhausted, and the house will be a mess... and I'll just feel like I'm failing at everything. I'll think, "I'm not a good mom, I'm not a good partner, I'm not a good person." It's like, this constant voice in my head is telling me that I'm not doing enough, that I'm not good enough.

And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm going to lose my mind. Or, I'll be trying to get the laundry done, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed by the sheer amount of work that needs to be done. It's like, everything is just getting on top of me, and I don't know how to get out from under it all.

I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? Like, I'm just pretending to be a functioning adult, but really, I'm just winging it and hoping that no one notices how lost and overwhelmed I am. It's a really scary feeling, because I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make the feelings of overwhelm and anxiety go away. I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of stress and worry, and I don't know how to escape.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. It's like, my mind is always racing, and I just can't seem to shut it off. I'll lie in bed, and I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and unhappiness. It's like, I'm just so consumed by my thoughts and emotions that I just can't relax and fall asleep.

Sometimes, I'll be awake for hours in the middle of the night, just lying there and thinking about everything that's going on. I'll think about the baby, and I'll worry about whether I'm doing everything right. I'll think about my relationship with my husband, and I'll worry about whether we're going to be okay. I'll think about my own identity, and I'll worry about whether I'm losing myself in all of this.

It's hard to explain, but it feels like my mind is just constantly churning, and I just can't seem to calm it down. And when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often have these really vivid and disturbing dreams. I'll dream about the baby getting hurt, or about something terrible happening to my family. It's like, my subconscious is just processing all of these fears and anxieties, and it's manifesting in these really intense and unsettling dreams.

I've tried everything to help me sleep, from warm baths to meditation to reading before bed. But nothing seems to work for long. I'll have a good night's sleep, and then I'll be back to lying awake and worrying. It's just so exhausting, you know? I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank.

It's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, though. It's the emotional toll that it's taking on me. I feel like I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, and I don't know how to find my way back.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I have a beautiful baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but at the same time, I just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and emptiness. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and doing all the things I'm supposed to do, but I'm not really feeling anything. I'm not feeling happy, I'm not feeling fulfilled, I'm just feeling empty and sad.

Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. I'll be feeding her, or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and I don't know how to deal with them. I'll try to talk to my husband about it, but I don't know how to explain how I'm feeling. I'll just say something like, "I'm just feeling really overwhelmed," or "I'm just feeling really sad," but it's hard to put into words.

It's not just the big things that are getting to me, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and she'll just cry and cry, and I'll feel like I'm failing her. Or, I'll be trying to make dinner, and I'll just feel so exhausted and overwhelmed, and I'll wonder how I'm going to get everything done. It's just like, everything is piling up on me, and I don't know how to deal with it.

I've been feeling really hopeless lately, too. Like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just think, "What's the point of all this?" or "I'll never be a good mom." It's like, these negative thoughts just keep swirling around in my head, and I don't know how to make them stop. I feel like I'm just drowning in my own emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

It's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just losing myself in all of this. I'm not the same person I was before I had the baby, and I don't know how to get back to being that person. I feel like I'm just a shell of my former self, and I don't know how to fill myself back up. I just feel so sad and miserable, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just because I'm tired or overwhelmed. It's like, I'm just feeling this deep sadness and emotional pain, and it's manifesting in tears. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. Or, I'll be doing something mundane like laundry or dishes, and I'll just break down in tears.

It's hard to explain, but it feels like I'm just so emotional and raw right now. Everything just feels so much more intense, and I don't know how to deal with it. I'll be watching a commercial on TV, and I'll just start crying because it's so sad. Or, I'll be reading a book, and I'll just start crying because it's so beautiful. It's like, my emotions are just so close to the surface, and I don't know how to keep them in check.

I've been trying to hide it from my husband, but it's hard. He'll come home from work, and I'll just be sitting there, crying, and he'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel so sad." And he'll try to comfort me, but it's hard to explain why I'm feeling this way.

It's not just the crying that's the problem, it's the feeling of sadness and emptiness that's underlying it. I feel like I'm just so unhappy, and I don't know how to make it stop. I've been trying to do things that I used to enjoy, like going for walks or reading books, but nothing seems to be working. I just feel like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.

Sometimes, I'll be crying, and I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just be happy?" And then I'll feel guilty for feeling that way, because I know I'm supposed to be grateful for my baby and my life. But it's hard to feel grateful when you're feeling so sad and overwhelmed all the time.

I just wish I could find a way to make the crying stop, and to feel happy again. I wish I could find a way to deal with all these emotions, and to feel like myself again. But for now, I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of sadness and tears, and I don't know how to escape.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
